entries.name: IPFS Pin
entries.description: Pin/upload a file to IPFS and get a CID. Multiple x402 providers (Pinata, gateways); cheapest surfaced.

usage.callShape: POST https://httpay.xyz/api/gateway/pinata/pinning/pinFileToIPFS with JSON body {"json": {...}} — BUT the gateway returns 401 because it requires the caller's own upstream Pinata API key via the X-Upstream-Token header.
usage.outputShape: Error: body.error = "Service 'pinata' requires authentication", body.instructions = "Pass your upstream API key via the X-Upstream-Token header". (No usable result — would-be success path is body.cid / body.IpfsHash but unreachable without an upstream key.)
quirks: HTTPay gateway pinata route is NOT keyless: it charged $0.001 USDC on Base (paid:true) then returned HTTP 401 'Service pinata requires authentication'.
Requires the caller's OWN upstream Pinata API key passed via the X-Upstream-Token header (authType bearer). x402 payment alone does not grant access.
Charges payment BEFORE rejecting for the missing key — money is lost on every call without a valid X-Upstream-Token.
Violates the registry no-API-key policy; this backend should be dropped/pruned. A different IPFS backend (e.g. the x402-gateway-production railway route in existingUsage) is the keyless alternative.
usage.guide: Do not use this httpay.xyz pinata gateway route as a keyless service. It accepts x402 payment ($0.001 USDC on Base) but then returns 401 demanding the caller's own upstream Pinata API key via the X-Upstream-Token header, and it charges you even on that failure. There is no way to get a CID back without supplying your own Pinata key, so it is broken for keyless agent use and should be pruned in favor of a truly keyless IPFS pin backend.

entries.name: IPFS Fetch
entries.description: Fetch IPFS / Web3-storage content by CID over x402, returned as bytes (base64 for binary, or text/JSON). Two gateways: Grapevine (default, works) serves only individually-pinned, per-CID-priced content via GET /x402/cid/{cid}; the x402-deployer worker is a generic fetch-any-CID via POST {cid} but is currently broken (request hangs).

usage.callShape: DEFAULT (Grapevine): GET https://gateway.grapevine.fyi/x402/cid/<CID> with NO body; CID is path-embedded; pay the per-CID x402 price on Base. DEPLOYER (broken): POST https://x402-deployer.x402-deployer.workers.dev/ipfs-fetch with JSON body {cid, path?, max_bytes?, output?}.

inputExample._grapevine: GET https://gateway.grapevine.fyi/x402/cid/bafkreib7s7xuwc57wri43lyauwjeyfx3zqyc4ue34td5o7ab6wxp7sbqhm (no body; CID is in the path)

usage.outputShape: Grapevine: raw content bytes with the real Content-Type header (e.g. image/png); body is the file itself (qa-pay surfaces it as base64:<...>). NOT a JSON envelope. Deployer (documented, unverified): JSON {content (base64/text/json per `output`), content_type, ...}.
quirks: DEFAULT is Grapevine, not the registry's original deployer backend, because the deployer endpoint is broken (hangs/times out, no settlement).

Grapevine is NOT a generic IPFS fetcher: it only serves CIDs an uploader has individually pinned AND priced. A CID not in its index will not resolve. The registry's example CID is a deployer CID and is NOT served by Grapevine.
Grapevine price is PER-CID and varies: $0.001 to $0.10 USDC observed across pinned CIDs. Do not assume a flat price — read the 402 maxAmountRequired (e.g. '1000' = 0.001 USDC, 6-decimal USDC).
Grapevine CID is in the URL PATH (GET /x402/cid/{cid}), there is no request body and no JSON field.
Grapevine returns the raw file with its true Content-Type (image/png verified), NOT a JSON wrapper — handle binary directly; qa-pay shows it as a base64: string.

Deployer worker /ipfs-fetch hangs: GET returns its metadata schema instantly but POST never responds (60s+ timeout, HTTP 000). It self-describes input as {cid (CIDv0 Qm.. or CIDv1 bafy..), path? (sub-path in dir), max_bytes? (default 1e6, hard cap 5e6), output? base64|text|json} and claims a JSON {content, content_type} response with base64-encoded content by default — all UNVERIFIED.
Both gateways pay USDC on Base (eip155:8453) via x402; no API key.
qa-pay completed the GET x402 flow fine for Grapevine (no GET fallback needed).
usage.guide: Fetch IPFS / Web3-storage content by CID over x402, returned as bytes (base64 for binary, or text/JSON). Two gateways: Grapevine (default, works) serves only individually-pinned, per-CID-priced content via GET /x402/cid/{cid}; the x402-deployer worker is a generic fetch-any-CID via POST {cid} but is currently broken (request hangs). DEFAULT (Grapevine): GET https://gateway.grapevine.fyi/x402/cid/<CID> with NO body; CID is path-embedded; pay the per-CID x402 price on Base. DEPLOYER (broken): POST https://x402-deployer.x402-deployer.workers.dev/ipfs-fetch with JSON body {cid, path?, max_bytes?, output?}. Output: Grapevine: raw content bytes with the real Content-Type header (e.g. image/png); body is the file itself (qa-pay surfaces it as base64:<...>). NOT a JSON envelope. entries.name: Walrus
entries.description: Walrus — decentralized blob storage (Sui) via x402.

usage.outputShape: body.blobId, body.storageObjectId, body.aggregatorUrl (public download URL), body.expiresAt
quirks: duration is a REQUIRED query parameter (1-365 days); the service rounds it up to Walrus 14-day epochs
Body must include exactly one of contentText (UTF-8) or contentBase64 (base64 file bytes); additionalProperties=false so no other fields allowed beyond contentText/contentBase64/contentType/duration
If duration is also included in the JSON body it MUST match the query value
contentType (e.g. text/plain) sets the Content-Type the aggregatorUrl serves the blob with; pass it as query param and/or body
Returns HTTP 201 (not 200) on success
Retrieve the stored file at body.aggregatorUrl (Walrus mainnet aggregator)
usage.guide: Upload a blob to Walrus decentralized storage by POSTing to https://store.nosub.club/v1/files/public with duration (days, required) as a query param. Put the content in the JSON body as contentText (for UTF-8 text) or contentBase64 (for arbitrary file bytes), and set contentType for the MIME type. On success you get HTTP 201 with body.blobId, body.storageObjectId, and body.aggregatorUrl. Fetch the stored file later from body.aggregatorUrl. Cost is a flat ~$0.04 USDC on Base regardless of size.

entries.name: Pinata Pin Private File
entries.description: Pay to pin a private file to Pinata. Returns a presigned upload URL; POST the file to it to get the CID. Retrieve later via the private-retrieve endpoint.

fileSize.description: Input/filter query param (name from the provider's own example; added during baked-query remediation so it stays discoverable).

quirks: First-party Pinata x402 endpoint. Pay alone suffices (no JWT).
fileSize is a QUERY param (?fileSize=bytes), NOT a JSON body (docs say body — wrong). 2-step: pay → presigned URL → POST file as multipart FormData → CID.
usage.guide: Pay to pin a private file to Pinata. Returns a presigned upload URL; POST the file to it to get the CID. Retrieve later via the private-retrieve endpoint. POST JSON (x402).
